title: Investigating the Nano-Scale Distribution of Alloying Elements in Zircaloy-4 Using High Resolution Characterization Techniques
content: Zircaloy-4, a zirconium (Zr)-based alloy, has been extensively employed as a nuclear fuel cladding material in light water reactors (LWRs) due to its remarkable properties such as low neutron absorption cross-section, high corrosion resistance, and good mechanical strength [1]. Neutron irradiation leads to the formation of radiation-induced defects, such as dislocation loops, voids, and precipitates, which can significantly affect the dimensional stability of the alloy, tensile strength, and creep resistance [2, 3]. Understanding these irradiation effects is essential for predicting performance and developing strategies to mitigate degradation. The distribution of alloying elements, such as tin (Sn), iron (Fe), and chromium (Cr), in Zircaloy-4 plays a pivotal role in determining its microstructural characteristics and corrosion behavior.
